thread:
laura: secbot just flagged a suspicious chain on tyler-laptop — chrome extension spawned a native binary and opened remote connections. can someone pick this up?

secbot: ALERT: EDR ID 0x9f3a
- host: TYLER-LAPTOP
- user: tyler@redwood.ai
- detection: suspicious child process spawn (chrome.exe -> walletd.exe)
- path: C:\Users\tyler\AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Extensions\gldfpekaef
- process cmd: \"C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe /c \"%LOCALAPPDATA%\WalletSvc\walletd.exe\" -r\"
- connections: outbound to 45.76.18.9:443 and wallet-sync.example[.]com:8545
- action: quarantine attempted, process killed, extension disabled

tyler: oh wow. i did install a new wallet extension this morning (name: QuickPocket). i thought it was legit from chrome store.

mira: thanks laura. quick questions: did secbot capture a triage bundle (proc memory + browser profile)?

secbot: triage-bot created snapshot: /var/edr/triage/TYLER-LAPTOP-2005006789.zip (0.8GB). IEM logs included.

ashok: copying the important bits — can someone confirm whether any AWS/GCP keys or KMS calls were made from that host? if the extension accessed local files we need to rotate any exposed creds.

kevin: i'll check cloud audit logs for any KMS decrypt/iam activity from tyler's identity. also flagging IAM service token rotations.

laura: we should treat this as possible credential exposure. isolate the laptop from network until we confirm. tyler, can you disconnect ethernet/wifi and leave laptop powered on?

tyler: disconnected. laptop off VPN too. i'm not doing heavy dev work atm.

mira: good. as next steps: 1) forensics team to pull image, 2) revoke any long-lived tokens on tyler's machine (PATs, cloud creds), 3) rotate KMS credentials if any key material was used, 4) reimage laptop.

ashok: for step 2 i'll list ~/.aws/ credentials, GCP ADC locations, and check browser stored credentials. can someone grant me temporary sudo for the host?

laura: granting via jumpbox now, will msg you creds in DM.

kevin: cloud logs show an API call to kms:Decrypt for key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01 around 09:12 UTC, from IP 3.120.45.22. that's from our build runner normally, not tyler. need correlation.

mira: ok that KMS call is suspiciously timed. add it to incident ticket. as precaution, rotate any customer-facing service keys that might be accessible.

secbot: file hash info: walletd.exe MD5: d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e (placeholder) — sample uploaded to sandbox: https://malware-sandbox.internal/submit/2005006789

tyler: extension name and ID look fake now — i just removed QuickPocket from chrome; should i also clear browser profile?

mira: do not clear yet, we need the profile for artifacts. leave it unchanged. we'll create a clean copy for your new browser.

laura: triage ask: forensics to collect browser extension folder, Pref and Local State, and network pcap if possible. triage-bot already captured process list and open sockets.

kevin: i've opened ticket SEC-INC-2026-045 and added initial timeline + cloud logs. tagging infra-oncall for potential key rotations.

ashok: starting live memory capture now. will push for full disk image if we find persistence.

mira: decision: recommended action = reimage + rotate credentials + enterprise password reset for any reused passwords. also run org-wide scan for QuickPocket extension signature.

laura: communication: i'll post a short notice in #incidents and ping legal if user data touched. aim to update in 2 hours. :hourglass: 

tyler: thanks all. let me know if you need my laptop physically shipped or any approvals.

laura: we'll advise after forensics. for now no shipping — keep device isolated.

triage-bot: follow-up scheduled: 2005007600 (forensics update).

mira: assigning owner for post-incident actions: laura (comms), ashok (forensics), kevin (cloud/RBAC), tyler (affected user contact).
